Section: Stage 01 - Enter the unseen world
Subject: Surface world / starting point
Body: We begin in the visible world at the drilling rig. This establishes the real operational context before moving into the hidden subsurface environment.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 01 - Enter the unseen world
Subject: Descending from the rig
Body: The camera follows the drill string downward, moving from the offshore surface through the water and toward the seabed. This begins the transition from the visible world into the unseen world below.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 01 - Enter the unseen world
Subject: Through earth layers
Body: We are now underground, following the drill string through the subsurface. This panel establishes the hidden geological world where direct human vision is no longer possible.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 01 - Enter the unseen world
Subject: Deep underground / ECCO in darkness
Body: We arrive deep underground near ECCO. The environment is dark and inaccessible. This establishes the core problem: the well cannot simply be “looked at” directly, which is why ECCO’s sensing capability is needed.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 02 - Reveal the principle
Subject: First pulse
Body: ECCO begins the measurement process by sending one ultrasonic pulse outward toward the borehole wall. This introduces the basic sensing principle.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 02 - Reveal the principle
Subject: Echo returns
Body: The pulse reflects from the borehole wall and returns to ECCO. This is the crucial pulse-echo step: ECCO measures by transmitting and then listening.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 02 - Reveal the principle
Subject: One measurement point
Body: One pulse and one returned echo produce one measured point on the wall. At this stage, ECCO is not creating an optical image — it is building measurement data.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 02 - Reveal the principle
Subject: More pulses while rotating
Body: As the drill string rotates, ECCO rotates with it. More pulses are sent in different directions, and more measured points accumulate around the borehole wall.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 02 - Reveal the principle
Subject: One complete ring
Body: After enough rotation and repeated pulse-echo measurements, one circular ring of wall data is formed at that depth. This is the basic unit of ECCO’s borehole reconstruction.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 03 - Open Hole : Geometry & Formation Imaging
Subject: Ideal borehole diameter
Body: We begin with the expected borehole diameter based on the drill bit size. The circular reference represents the intended hole size before comparing it with the actual underground conditions.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 03 - Open Hole : Geometry & Formation Imaging
Subject: Actual borehole geometry / washout
Body:
As drilling progresses, the surrounding formation may break away or become enlarged, creating an irregular hole known as washout.


ECCO measures the distance to the wall in different directions, allowing the actual borehole shape to be compared with the intended diameter. The highlighted section represents an enlarged area.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 03 - Open Hole : Geometry & Formation Imaging
Subject: Geometry through depth
Body:
As ECCO rotates and travels through the well, measurements are collected at successive depths.


These measurements are combined to reconstruct the changing borehole geometry, including enlarged, narrowed or irregular sections.


The result is a continuous 3D representation of the actual drilled hole.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 03 - Open Hole : Geometry & Formation Imaging
Subject: The same echo provides another measurement
Body:
The same ultrasonic echo used to calculate distance also carries information about the strength of the reflected signal.
ECCO analyses two properties:
• Time of Flight: How long the echo takes to return, used to determine distance and borehole geometry.
• Amplitude: The strength of the reflected echo, providing information about acoustic variations along the formation wall.



These are two different measurements extracted from the ultrasonic response.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 03 - Open Hole : Geometry & Formation Imaging
Subject: Amplitude becomes a formation image
Body:
As ECCO rotates and moves through depth, amplitude measurements accumulate around the borehole wall.


These measurements are arranged into a continuous 360° image, displayed using different color shades to represent variations in the ultrasonic reflections.


The resulting formation image helps geologists identify patterns and changes in the surrounding rock. The colors represent measured acoustic responses, not the actual color of the formation.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 04 - Cased Hole : Cement Evaluation & Casing Integrity
Subject: From open hole to cased hole
Body:
We transition from the open-hole environment into a cased-hole environment.
In a cased well, a steel pipe has been installed inside the drilled hole, with cement placed in the space between the casing and surrounding rock.


ECCO now measures the steel casing rather than the exposed rock wall. This introduces its additional well-integrity applications.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 04 - Cased Hole : Cement Evaluation & Casing Integrity
Subject: Ultrasonic interaction with steel casing
Body:
ECCO sends an ultrasonic pulse outward toward the inner surface of the steel casing.
The sound interacts with the steel, producing a reflected signal and exciting a vibration or ringing response within the casing wall.

ECCO records the returning acoustic response, which can provide information about the condition of the casing and its surrounding cement.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 04 - Cased Hole : Cement Evaluation & Casing Integrity
Subject: Cement support changes the casing response
Body:
The way the steel casing vibrates depends partly on how it is supported by the material behind it.

When cement is properly bonded to the casing, the surrounding material generally damps the vibration more quickly.
Where cement bonding is poor or support is missing, the casing may continue ringing for longer.

By analysing differences in the returning ultrasonic response, ECCO can help evaluate cement condition behind the casing.

The two waveforms illustrate the principle, not exact diagnostic signals.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 04 - Cased Hole : Cement Evaluation & Casing Integrity
Subject: Building a 360° cement evaluation map
Body:
As ECCO collects ultrasonic measurements around the casing and through depth, the recorded responses can be processed into a continuous 360° cement evaluation map.

This helps engineers assess variations in cement bonding around the casing and identify areas that may require further investigation.

The visual transitions from the cylindrical casing into a flat, unwrapped engineering map.

Colors are illustrative and do not represent the actual Mi-VU cement evaluation color scale.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 04 - Cased Hole : Cement Evaluation & Casing Integrity
Subject: Casing integrity: detecting wear and deformation
Body:
Beyond cement evaluation, ECCO can also examine the internal geometry of the steel casing.

By measuring the ultrasonic travel time to the casing's inner wall, ECCO can assess changes in the casing's internal profile.
The illustration compares a normal circular casing interior with a locally enlarged or worn section.

These measurements can help identify potential casing wear, deformation or irregularities that may affect well integrity.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 05 - Hydraulic Enhancement
Subject: The circulation path
Body: Drilling mud is pumped down through the inside of the drill string and exits through the drill bit. It then returns toward the surface through the annular space between the outside of the drill string and the borehole wall, carrying drilled rock cuttings. This establishes the direction of flow before we examine ECCO's hydraulic body features.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 05 - Hydraulic Enhancement
Subject: Hydraulic accelerator pads
Body: The first hydraulic function comes from accelerator pads built into ENP3's outer geometry. As returning mud flows around these raised surfaces, its local velocity increases, helping to lift and transport cuttings through the annulus. The illustrated pad and streamlines are conceptual rather than an exact cross-section or flow simulation.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 05 - Hydraulic Enhancement
Subject: Twisted pads
Body: Two sets of twisted pads are designed to redirect and agitate the surrounding mud, producing local jetting and controlled turbulence that help prevent rock cuttings from settling into beds. The twisting action is provided by the physical geometry; according to the datasheet, it can contribute during rotation, axial tool movement, and/or circulating mud.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 05 - Hydraulic Enhancement
Subject: Diffuser
Body: After the accelerated and agitated flow passes the pads, the diffuser shapes its exit path to recover pressure and reduce the low-pressure wake where cuttings could otherwise gather. This is intended to lower the risk of accumulation and pack-off. The visual shows the intended flow principle, not verified computational fluid dynamics.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 05 - Hydraulic Enhancement
Subject: Three stages working together
Body: The camera pulls back to reveal that Stage 1 (accelerator), Stage 2 (twisted pads) and Stage 3 (diffuser) are not separate operating modes. They are three integrated functional sections of the ENP3 body. As mud moves through the annulus it encounters them in sequence; fluid flows through all sections continuously and each contributes to cuttings transport and hole cleaning.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 1) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: Recorded measurements become Mi-VU outputs
Body: ECCO records detailed ultrasonic measurements in the tool during the run. After the tool is retrieved, the stored information can be processed using MIT's Mi-VU software. The animation moves away from the downhole environment and into real engineering analysis. This transition represents post-run processing, not a live data transmission to the surface.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 1) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: Hole diameter and circular cross-sections
Body: The first recognizable Mi-VU outputs are the hole-diameter curves and circular cross-sections. The diameter track shows how the measured hole size changes through depth. Cross-sections show the shape of the borehole at selected depths. These visuals are simplified interpretations of the report's Hole Diameter MIN/AVG/MAX and Cross Section — RIH tracks.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 1) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: Building the 3D hole image
Body: The measurements from successive depths are combined into a continuous representation of the borehole. The look transitions from our dramatic 3D animation to the pale-blue, vertically striated style of Mi-VU's 3D Hole Image track. This demonstrates how a series of local measurements becomes a view of the complete measured interval.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 1) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: The 360-degree measurement tracks
Body: Mi-VU also presents measurements as flat, 360-degree images that run continuously through depth. The provided field report includes separate Hole Size — RIH and Hole Size — POOH tracks, a 4D Variance track and an Amplitude track. The blue-toned panels represent hole-size variation; the brown panel represents measured acoustic amplitude. These colors are not photographs or natural rock colors.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 1) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: Reveal the real Mi-VU field log
Body: The individual visualizations now resolve into the complete engineering log, using the same track order and visual conventions seen in MIT's supplied report. Ideally, the final animation should finish this section by transitioning from our simplified graphic to a genuine Mi-VU report or software capture provided by MIT. The supplied LipanBara example is labelled ENP1, so it should not be presented as verified ENP3 field-test output.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 2) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: The measurements are retrieved
Body:
After ECCO is retrieved from the well, its stored ultrasonic measurements are downloaded for processing.We visualize the invisible recorded information as streams of light emerging from the tool. 

This is a cinematic representation of stored data being accessed, not real-time transmission from underground.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 2) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: Measurements begin forming structure
Body:
The stored ultrasonic measurements are processed and organized according to their recorded positions and depths.

Abstract points begin forming a continuous representation of the borehole, showing how individual measurements can contribute to an understanding of the underground structure.

This is a stylized data visualization, not a literal view of the Mi-VU software.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 2) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: Two different types of information
Body:
ECCO's ultrasonic recordings support two complementary forms of analysis.
The measurements of echo travel time can be used to reconstruct borehole geometry, while the strength of the returning signal can be mapped to reveal acoustic variations along the formation.

In this scene, the two outputs appear side by side as stylized visualizations: blue for geometry and warm tones for amplitude.

They are separate interpretations of recorded echoes, not one image being converted into the other.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 2) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: The visualizations come together
Body:
The stylized geometry and amplitude visualizations converge toward a single presentation of the processed measurements.

This is the transition from our cinematic explanation to MIT's real engineering software.

At the end of the shot, we move directly into actual Mi-VU field output.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Stage 06 (Option 2) - From invisible measurements to real engineering output
Subject: Reveal the actual Mi-VU field log
Body:
The final frame reveals an actual engineering report generated by MIT's Mi-VU software using recorded ECCO-family measurements.
The report brings together borehole diameter, circular cross-sections, 3D hole geometry, 360° hole-size images, variance and amplitude in one engineering presentation.

This creates a direct connection between the sensing principles demonstrated in the animation and their practical engineering applications.

Reference: LipanBara field report, ENP1. The supplied data should be used with MIT's approval.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Section 07 - Product Hero / Closing
Subject: The results lead back to ECCO
Body: We move away from the final Mi-VU field log and reveal the physical ECCO ENP3. The camera connects the engineering information shown in the previous scene with the tool behind the measurements. This links the data output to the hardware rather than introducing a new capability. The transition is conceptual; the field data is processed after tool retrieval.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Section 07 - Product Hero / Closing
Subject: Complete product hero
Body: The technical charts and supporting visuals fade away, leaving a clean, confident view of ECCO ENP3. We emphasize that ultrasonic measurement and hydraulic enhancement belong to one integrated downhole tool. The final 3D model should use MIT-approved CAD and accurate product geometry; this drawing is a storyboard placeholder.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Section 07 - Product Hero / Closing
Subject: Five capabilities, one integrated solution
Body: Five familiar visual symbols briefly appear around ECCO ENP3, recalling what the audience has already learned: wellbore geometry, formation imaging, cement evaluation, casing integrity and hydraulic enhancement. This is a visual summary, not five new explanations. The final motion may introduce the labels in post-production if approved by MIT.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)

Section: Section 07 - Product Hero / Closing
Subject: MIT Technologies closing identity
Body: The five capability symbols fade out. We finish with the complete ECCO ENP3 product and the official MIT Technologies logo, including its existing tagline. This is the final brand impression. The supplied MIT logo has been included without altering its content or proportions.
Author: Radz (radziamin91)
